clue.text: A 19th-century novel in which an editor's contributions are more evident than usual

definitions.text: A 19th-century novel in which an editor's contributions are more evident than usual

parts.words: A 19th-century novel in which an editor's contributions are more evident than usual
parts.note: Carlyle's 1830s book poses as a German philosopher's work stitched together and commented on by a fictional editor, whose voice dominates the text

explanation.surface: A Victorian novel where the editor's hand shows more than it normally would.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlyle's book, whose Latin title means 'the tailor re-tailored', is framed as an editor's patchwork of a fictional professor's papers, so the editor is unusually visible.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle's work of 1833-34 is a satirical novel built around an intrusive fictional editor.

clue.text: Councillor welcomed by a consular agent in the capital of Guinea

indicators.note: one thing welcomed by another is taken in, so the councillor goes inside the agent

parts.note: CA is an abbreviation for consular agent

explanation.surface: A local councillor is received by a consular official in a West African capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinea here is the old name for the West African coast along the Gulf of Guinea, not the modern republic, whose capital is Conakry; Ghana's capital lies on that coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana's capital is a port on the Gulf of Guinea, the coast long called Guinea by Europeans.

clue.text: White men arrive in this hectic night — it includes dive serving up gin

indicators.note: a hectic scene is chaotic, so the letters of night are thrown into a new order
the word it is wrapped around the dive, which sits inside

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
to dive is to fall

indicators.note: in a down clue, serving something up turns it upwards, so the word for gin reads bottom to top

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: A frantic evening where a seedy bar ends up dishing out gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hectic' rearranges NIGHT into THING; 'includes' puts FALL in SA; 'serving up' turns TRAP into PART. Achebe's novel tells of the arrival of white missionaries and colonisers in an Igbo village.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinua Achebe's novel depicts colonial missionaries coming to a Nigerian village and its consequences.

clue.text: South coast town with a reputation for smuggling whiskey

definitions.text: South coast town with a reputation for smuggling
definitions.meaning: a small town in East Sussex, England, once a notorious haunt of smugglers
a whiskey distilled mainly from this grain, popular in North America

explanation.surface: A seaside town known for running contraband liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sussex Cinque Port was a smugglers' haven, and the same word names a North American spirit.

clue.text: "The sooner the Crown Colony system is (..) put under a glass case in the South Kensington museum, labelled '—', the better for everyone" (MaryKingsley)

definitions.text: "The sooner the Crown Colony system is (..) put under a glass case in the South Kensington museum, labelled '—', the better for everyone" (MaryKingsley)

parts.words: "The sooner the Crown Colony system is (..) put under a glass case in the South Kensington museum, labelled '—', the better for everyone" (MaryKingsley)
parts.note: the missing museum label is the word for a species that has died out, as on a fossil exhibit in the Natural History Museum

explanation.surface: The Victorian explorer Mary Kingsley wishes colonial rule were displayed in a museum as a dead specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: The South Kensington museum is London's Natural History Museum, where vanished creatures such as dinosaurs are displayed under glass with a label.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum label for something no longer living anywhere, like the dodo, completes Kingsley's jibe at colonial government.

clue.text: Scottish author of a story about network service

indicators.note: the story goes about, that is around, the next two pieces

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib
LAN stands for local area network
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A Scottish writer's tale concerning a computer network maintenance job.
explanation.walkthrough: The network and service run together as LANMASS inside LIE, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish novelist and journalist wrote historical fiction about Rome and Scotland.

clue.text: A book misrepresenting the East Indies, or one including birth, marriage and death

indicators.note: to misrepresent something is to present it wrongly, so the letters of the phrase are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A travel book giving a false picture of the East Indies, or a family saga spanning a lifetime.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes 'the East Indies, or' (15 letters). The closing phrase describes Carol Shields's novel, which follows Daisy Goodwill from her birth through marriage to her death.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol Shields's Pulitzer-winning novel is a well-known literary work, a fictional life story.

clue.text: One artist's changing paper supplier

indicators.note: changing letters around produces a new arrangement of them

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A painter switches to a different shop for their paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's is a letter here: ONE plus ARTISTS gives the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop or person selling writing paper, envelopes and pens is a seller of paper goods.

clue.text: Unplanned love for one in Western? Just the reverse

indicators.note: one thing put for another stands in its place, here a swap of letters
the swap runs the other way from how it reads: one replaces love rather than love replacing one

parts.note: occidental means western
love is zero in tennis, so O
A means one

explanation.surface: An unexpected romance in a cowboy film, or so the clue teases before turning it round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, 'love for one in Western' would put O for A; 'Just the reverse' says put A for the O of OCCIDENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accidental happens by chance, without design or intention.

clue.text: Maybe promotion that surprises me

parts.note: e.g., for example, signals that something is maybe one case
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: Someone startled by a sales promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned exclamation of astonishment, a mild oath like 'gosh'.

clue.text: Fringe English teacher gave lecture

parts.note: bangs are the American word for a fringe of hair
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A peripheral English master delivered a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To bang on is British slang for talking at tedious length, as in a lecture.

clue.text: Service lines and balls may be hard to perceive with these at Wimbledon

definitions.text: Service lines and balls may be hard to perceive with these at Wimbledon

parts.words: Service lines and balls may be hard to perceive with these at Wimbledon
parts.note: sunglasses dim the view, so lines and balls on court are harder to see through them

explanation.surface: Tennis players struggle to see the court markings while wearing certain eyewear.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship, often played in summer sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinted spectacles cut glare but also make fine detail harder to see.

clue.text: A girl who goes to Africa to ensnare Bond

definitions.text: A girl who goes to Africa

parts.note: to net is to ensnare
a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: A young woman travels to Africa to trap James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like the spy but is just a tie. In Alice Walker's The Color Purple, Celie's sister goes to Africa as a missionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Celie's sister in Alice Walker's novel is a female character who works as a missionary in Africa.

clue.text: A Canadian author's novel or a British author's autobiography?

definitions.meaning: Yann Martel's first novel, published in 1996
an autobiography is a life told by oneself, and the British novelist Will shares this surname

explanation.surface: Asking whether a book is a Canadian's fiction or a Briton's memoir.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: Will Self is a British author, so a memoir by him is a book by Self.
explanation.definitionFit: Martel titled his novel with the word for one's own person, the very subject of any memoir.

clue.text: Kind of rule in favour of endlessly strict writer

parts.note: an em rule is a printer's dash, so em is a kind of rule
for means in favour of

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: stern means strict

explanation.surface: A strict writer argues in favour of some typographic rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of rule' looks like a principle but is the printer's em rule, a long dash.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist of A Passage to India and Howards End was a celebrated author.

clue.text: Writing possibly in keeping with new lessons to be learned

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, so the letter sits inside the word for keeping

parts.note: keeping means retaining
writing is one of the three Rs, so R

explanation.surface: Writing might be in line with fresh instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so writing can be R.
explanation.definitionFit: Retraining is fresh instruction to acquire new skills.

clue.text: Substance seen by silly fool among American folk with outlandish beliefs

indicators.note: the pieces go among, that is inside, the American abbreviation
silly suggests the letters are muddled into nonsense

parts.note: the gist is the substance of something

explanation.surface: A foolish person's essence is noticed by Americans with strange ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen by' just sets the substance beside the scrambled fool; 'among' then puts both inside the American abbreviation. Folk with outlandish beliefs here are those convinced of flying-saucer visits.
explanation.definitionFit: People who study flying saucers and alien visitors are believers in far-fetched ideas.

clue.text: A star may indicate this person in a novel with improvisation

definitions.text: A star may indicate this person

parts.note: Rider Haggard's adventure novel She
a riff is an improvised musical phrase

explanation.surface: A star marks someone in a book with improvised passages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests celebrity, but it is the badge worn by a Western lawman.
explanation.definitionFit: A Western lawman wears a star-shaped badge that shows his office.

clue.text: His best-known poem included a talking horse, "Mr Ed"

definitions.text: His best-known poem included a talking horse, "Mr Ed"

parts.words: His best-known poem included a talking horse, "Mr Ed"
parts.note: the American poet called Ed wrote the long poem Gunslinger, which features a talking horse, and the TV horse Mister Ed shares his first name

explanation.surface: A poet famed for a piece featuring the TV talking horse Mister Ed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mister Ed was an American sitcom horse; the poet Ed's epic Gunslinger has its own talking horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Dorn was an American Black Mountain poet whose epic Gunslinger is his most famous work.

clue.text: Fleet and Royal Marines in one family chronicle

indicators.note: the marines go in, so they are placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: A means one
Nabokov's novel Ada is subtitled A Family Chronicle

explanation.surface: A fleet and some Royal Marines feature in a single family history.
explanation.walkthrough: Ada or Ardor: A Family Chronicle is Nabokov's 1969 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, as in the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: "The road to the City of — is paved with yellow brick" (The Wonderful Wizard of Oz)

definitions.text: "The road to the City of — is paved with yellow brick" (The Wonderful Wizard of Oz)

parts.words: "The road to the City of — is paved with yellow brick" (The Wonderful Wizard of Oz)
parts.note: Baum's original text names Oz's capital after green gemstones, the city Dorothy heads for along the yellow brick road

explanation.surface: A line from Baum's Oz book about the yellow brick road.
explanation.definitionFit: In Baum's book Oz's capital is named for green precious stones, the gems that fill the city.

clue.text: Maybe Maltese grabbing royal ring is a violent gang member

indicators.note: the dog grabs the other pieces, holding them inside itself

parts.note: a Maltese is a breed of dog, so maybe a dog
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A Maltese person seizing a royal ring turns out to be a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maltese' looks like a person from Malta but is the toy dog breed. Droog is the word for a thug in Burgess's A Clockwork Orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Burgess coined the term for the young thugs in A Clockwork Orange, from Russian for friend.

clue.text: Pay back for something potentially explosive

indicators.note: back means the word is read from the end to the start

parts.note: to ante, or ante up, is to pay

explanation.surface: Paying something back for a possible bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ANTE into ETNA, the active volcano on Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily's active volcano could erupt at any time, so it may blow up.

clue.text: Biblical apostle who influenced Karl Marx?

definitions.meaning: one of the twelve apostles, either Peter or the Zealot, given his title
the French social theorist Henri de ..., an early socialist whose ideas Marx and Engels drew on

explanation.surface: Which apostle shaped Marx's thinking?
explanation.definitionFit: The name serves both the canonised disciple and the French utopian socialist count who inspired later socialists.

clue.text: What a tiger came for — a slice of gateau

indicators.note: a slice is a small part cut from the whole, so the letters sit within the word

explanation.surface: A tiger turns up for a piece of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Judith Kerr's children's book The Tiger Who Came to Tea has a tiger arrive at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: Judith Kerr's picture-book tiger arrives uninvited for an afternoon meal.

clue.text: Roaring Forties voyage in a nautical novel

indicators.note: roaring suggests wild disorder, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: a passage is a voyage by sea

explanation.surface: A sea novel set on a voyage through the stormy southern latitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roaring Forties are stormy latitudes of the Southern Ocean; here 'Roaring' rearranges FORTIES into RITESOF. William Golding's novel is set on a ship sailing to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: William Golding's Booker-winning novel takes place aboard a ship bound for Australia.
